title: HIV: starting and monitoring antiretroviral therapy (adult)
subject: infectious-disease
summary: Offer ART to everyone with confirmed HIV within 7 days of diagnosis (same day if ready) using TLD (tenofovir DF, lamivudine, dolutegravir) once daily, screen for TB and cryptococcal antigen when CD4 is low, give co-trimoxazole prophylaxis, and monitor viral load, switching only after confirmed failure.

sections.title: Rapid ART start
items: Offer ART to every adult with confirmed HIV, whatever the CD4 count. WHO: start within 7 days of diagnosis and offer same-day start to people who are ready; give priority to people with advanced HIV disease.

Confirm the diagnosis by the national testing algorithm before the first dose. Send CD4, viral load and safety bloods, but results need not be back before starting unless the history suggests TB or cryptococcal meningitis.

Before a rapid start, ask about cough, fever, weight loss, night sweats, headache and confusion. Investigate these first, because ART timing differs with TB meningitis and cryptococcal meningitis (see below).
Counsel on lifelong daily adherence, disclosure, condoms and partner testing. A sustained undetectable viral load means no sexual transmission.

sections.title: Baseline tests
items: CD4 count (defines advanced HIV disease and prophylaxis needs), HIV viral load, CBC, creatinine with eGFR, ALT, glucose, lipids and urinalysis.
HBsAg and anti-HCV. If HBsAg is positive or not yet known, the regimen must contain tenofovir plus lamivudine or emtricitabine.
Pregnancy test in women of childbearing potential, syphilis serology and STI screen, and cervical cancer screening.
TB screen at every visit (symptoms, chest X-ray, CRP or molecular test). Urine LF-LAM if CD4 200 or below (inpatient), 100 or below (outpatient), or any CD4 if seriously ill.
Serum or plasma cryptococcal antigen (CrAg) if CD4 is below 100 cells/mm3 (consider below 200). A positive CrAg needs a lumbar puncture to exclude meningitis.

DHHS: genotypic resistance testing (reverse transcriptase and protease) where available, plus integrase genotype after long-acting cabotegravir PrEP; do not delay ART for the result. HLA-B*5701 before any abacavir.

sections.title: First-line regimen
items: Preferred (WHO): TLD, tenofovir disoproxil fumarate 300 mg + lamivudine 300 mg + dolutegravir 50 mg as one tablet orally once daily. This includes women who are pregnant or may become pregnant.

DHHS regimens for most people: bictegravir/TAF/emtricitabine, or dolutegravir with TAF or TDF plus emtricitabine or lamivudine. Dolutegravir/lamivudine dual therapy only if viral load is 500,000 copies/mL or less, there is no hepatitis B, and genotype and HBV results are known.

If dolutegravir is unsuitable: TDF + lamivudine + efavirenz 400 mg once daily (WHO alternative; avoid where pretreatment NNRTI resistance is 10% or more or after previous ARV exposure), or a boosted protease inhibitor, with darunavir/ritonavir preferred (WHO 2025).
After long-acting cabotegravir PrEP, start boosted darunavir with tenofovir and lamivudine or emtricitabine until the integrase genotype is known (DHHS).
Do not start TDF if eGFR is below 50 mL/min, with uncontrolled hypertension or untreated diabetes (WHO); use abacavir (HLA-B*5701 negative) or TAF with lamivudine and dolutegravir.
Dolutegravir with rifampicin: increase to 50 mg twice daily (with TLD, add a separate dolutegravir 50 mg tablet 12 hours later). No change is needed with rifapentine (3HP).

Give dolutegravir 2 hours before or 6 hours after antacids and iron, calcium, magnesium or zinc supplements. Avoid high-dose metformin, and avoid carbamazepine, phenytoin and phenobarbital (use valproate or another alternative).

sections.title: Advanced HIV disease (CD4 below 200 or WHO stage 3 or 4)
items: Give the WHO package: rapid ART, TB screening with LF-LAM and molecular testing, CrAg screening, co-trimoxazole prophylaxis, TB preventive treatment once active TB is excluded, and pre-emptive fluconazole for CrAg-positive people.

Co-trimoxazole 960 mg (160/800 mg) orally once daily. WHO: CD4 350 or below, WHO stage 3 or 4, or active TB, and everyone where malaria or severe bacterial infections are common. US threshold: CD4 below 200 or oral candidiasis.

Stop co-trimoxazole (low malaria and bacterial infection settings) when clinically stable on ART with immune recovery and viral suppression (WHO); US criterion: CD4 above 200 for more than 3 months on ART.
CrAg positive, meningitis excluded: fluconazole 800 to 1200 mg daily for 2 weeks, then 800 mg daily for 8 weeks, then 200 mg daily maintenance. Start ART after 2 weeks of fluconazole.

TB preventive treatment once active TB is excluded: 3HP (weekly isoniazid 900 mg + rifapentine 900 mg for 12 weeks) is preferred (WHO 2025); 6 or 9 months of daily isoniazid is the alternative. Add pyridoxine.

sections.title: TB, meningitis and IRIS
items: Active TB (not meningitis): start TB treatment first, then ART as soon as possible within 2 weeks, whatever the CD4 count (WHO).
TB meningitis: delay ART for at least 4 weeks and start within 8 weeks of starting TB treatment (WHO). Give adjunctive corticosteroids for TB meningitis.
Cryptococcal meningitis: defer ART for 4 to 6 weeks from the start of antifungal therapy (see Cryptococcal meningitis protocol). Other OIs such as PCP: start ART within 2 weeks.

IRIS: paradoxical worsening of a treated infection, or unmasking of a new one, in the first weeks to months of ART, most often with a low baseline CD4. Continue ART, confirm the infection is adequately treated, and exclude drug resistance or a new diagnosis.
Treat mild IRIS symptomatically. Give corticosteroids for moderate to severe paradoxical TB IRIS only after other causes are excluded, with expert advice.

sections.title: Viral load monitoring and treatment failure
items: WHO: viral load by 6 months, at 12 months, then every 12 months once established on ART. DHHS: first viral load 4 to 8 weeks after starting, then every 4 to 8 weeks until below 50 copies/mL, then every 3 to 6 months.

Viral load above 1000 copies/mL: enhanced adherence support, check for interactions, vomiting or stock-outs, and repeat after 3 months. Low-level viraemia (50 to 1000 copies/mL): adherence counselling and repeat in 3 months.
Virological failure: two consecutive viral loads above 1000 copies/mL 3 months apart despite adherence support, after at least 6 months on ART (WHO).

Failing a dolutegravir regimen: switch to a boosted protease inhibitor (darunavir/ritonavir preferred, WHO 2025) with tenofovir and lamivudine; tenofovir can be recycled. Use resistance testing where available.
Where routine viral load is available, CD4 monitoring can stop once a person is established on ART and suppressed (WHO). Check creatinine regularly on TDF.

sections.title: Pregnancy, hepatitis B, simplification and India
items: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: start or continue a dolutegravir-based regimen at once, monitor viral load closely, and arrange infant prophylaxis (WHO 2025: 6 weeks of nevirapine for infants not at high risk; triple-drug prophylaxis if high risk).

Hepatitis B coinfection: always include TDF or TAF with lamivudine or emtricitabine. Never use dolutegravir/lamivudine alone, and do not stop tenofovir without expert advice (risk of hepatitis flare).
Stable and suppressed without hepatitis B: dolutegravir + lamivudine for simplification, or long-acting injectable cabotegravir + rilpivirine as an alternative switch (WHO 2025).
India: NACO ART centres provide free ART, CD4 and viral load testing, and TLD is the national first-line adult regimen. Link every new diagnosis to an ART centre.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Delaying ART for CD4 results or repeated readiness visits when the person is well and willing to start.
Starting ART immediately in cryptococcal or TB meningitis, which increases mortality.
Using dolutegravir/lamivudine dual therapy with hepatitis B or before viral load and genotype results.
Forgetting the rifampicin interaction (dolutegravir must be twice daily) or co-administering dolutegravir with antacids or iron.
Starting TB preventive treatment without excluding active TB.
Switching a dolutegravir regimen after a single high viral load without adherence support and a repeat test.

drugs.name: TLD (tenofovir DF + lamivudine + dolutegravir)
drugs.dose: 300 mg + 300 mg + 50 mg, one tablet orally once daily
drugs.notes: Preferred first-line (WHO, NACO). Avoid TDF if eGFR below 50 mL/min.

drugs.name: Dolutegravir (additional dose)
drugs.dose: 50 mg orally, taken 12 hours after TLD, while on rifampicin
drugs.notes: Gives dolutegravir 50 mg twice daily with rifampicin.

drugs.name: Bictegravir/TAF/emtricitabine
drugs.dose: 50/25/200 mg, one tablet orally once daily

drugs.name: Darunavir/ritonavir
drugs.dose: 800/100 mg orally once daily with food; 600/100 mg twice daily after protease inhibitor failure
drugs.notes: Preferred boosted PI (WHO 2025); many drug interactions.

drugs.name: Efavirenz
drugs.dose: 400 mg orally once daily with TDF + lamivudine
drugs.notes: WHO alternative first line; avoid with high NNRTI pretreatment resistance.

drugs.name: Co-trimoxazole
drugs.notes: Prophylaxis per WHO or US criteria above.

drugs.name: Fluconazole (pre-emptive)
drugs.dose: 800 to 1200 mg daily for 2 weeks, then 800 mg daily for 8 weeks, then 200 mg daily

drugs.name: Isoniazid + rifapentine (3HP)
drugs.dose: Isoniazid 900 mg + rifapentine 900 mg orally once weekly for 12 weeks
drugs.notes: Preferred TB preventive treatment in HIV (WHO 2025); give pyridoxine.
